decision: Generate a two-segment, four-channel full-span robot whose undeformed tip length matches the approximately 0.29 m targets. Use nearly matched bending stiffness across the root and repeated segment, external tendons at 0.020 m radius, zero pretension, and moderate discretization. Evaluate all four required conditions with slow piecewise-linear tension ramps to obtain directional response, terminal error, speed, and actuator-limit evidence before revising.
evidence: The task supplies four independent channels and every required condition specifies independent_channels=4, so the initial candidate uses exactly four tendons. The prototype straight length is approximately aligned with target x coordinates: segment_0 is 0.16 m, the intersegment guide/connector offset is about 0.014 m, segment_1 is 0.11 m, and the payload tip offset is 0.014 m. Targets primarily require transverse bending. The supplied root ellipse is substantially stiffer than the repeated rectangle at their default moduli, so root Young's modulus is reduced to 2.5 MPa while repeated-segment modulus is raised to 7.0 MPa to make curvature distribution less discontinuous. A full-span quadrature routing should provide signed y and z bending authority. Tensions start at the mandated 0 N and ramp gradually, which is expected to reduce excitation and tendon-speed violations while revealing channel signs and force sensitivity.

decision: Replace the numerically fragile baseline with a low-order, symmetric, moderately stiff circular two-segment arm while preserving the useful 0.298 m initial reach and four independent full-length tendons. Then probe only the upward M1_A motion with a slow 2 N ramp on the +z tendon to obtain a complete trajectory without mixing incompatible evaluator backends.
evidence: All three separate zero-input c1 reach runs became incomplete after only about 193 integration steps and reported COMPLETE_CORE_TASK_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED; thus c1 cannot provide authoritative full-duration evidence even with no actuation. Their shared initial observation was tip [0.298,0,0.15], which is well aligned in x with all targets, so length should be retained. The initial four-tendon geometry is also appropriate for the required four independent channels. A symmetric circular section removes prototype anisotropy, 10 MPa material and 10 mm radius increase robustness, and four cells per segment reduce high-frequency numerical modes. The M1_A target differs primarily by +z, so a gradual single-channel input is the cleanest sign and compliance test. Expected outcome is a complete 0.6 s run, upward tip displacement, and lower actuator-speed excitation than a step command.

decision: Measure c2's unactuated gravity response before changing structure or tuning upward actuation. This isolates how much of the observed downward motion and speed violation came from gravity versus the channel-1 tendon, and it identifies whether channel 3 must merely cancel gravity or also generate the full upward displacement.
evidence: In the completed c2 M1_A run, channel 1 tension produced motion almost exclusively in negative world z: tip z fell from 0.150 m initially to 0.069 m at 0.14 s and ended at 0.084 m under 2 N, while y remained near zero. The run remained solver-valid and within stroke, but holding speed was 0.457 m/s and tendon speed 0.0848 m/s. Because tension was still only 0.6 N at 0.14 s and gravity acts from the initial instant, the relative contributions are not yet known. Expected outcome is an authoritative passive trajectory establishing gravity sag, oscillation amplitude, and whether c2 can ever satisfy the 0.025 m/s tendon-speed constraint without structural stiffening.

decision: Replace the dynamically unusable c2 with a substantially stiffer, nearly isotropic two-segment arm while preserving the approximately 0.298 m straight reach needed by all targets. Use four full-length tendons at maximum routing radius for bidirectional planar bending, and immediately measure its passive gravity response before actuator mapping.
evidence: The latest authoritative c2 zero-input M1_A run showed that gravity alone moved the tip from [0.298,0,0.150] to z=0.0645 m by 0.14 s, with peak observed tip speed above 0.65 m/s, holding speed 0.427 m/s, and geometric tendon speed 0.0864 m/s. Thus control tuning alone cannot make c2 satisfy the 0.025 m/s geometric-speed limit robustly. A circular 0.010 m section, moderate 5 MPa modulus, and reduced six-cell model are expected to suppress gravity sag and high flexible modes while retaining enough compliance for 8 N tendons at 0.023 m radius to reach the required offsets.

decision: Use c3 to identify the vertical tendon direction and test whether active gravity cancellation can suppress the severe passive oscillation without another structural revision. Apply a smooth rise on the presumed +z tendon (channel 1 at phase pi/2), followed by reduced holding tension to avoid excessive upward overshoot.
evidence: The c3 passive run began at [0.298,0,0.150] and fell rapidly, reaching z=0.0437 m at 0.14 s with downward velocity -1.105 m/s, then oscillating through z=-0.0017 and z=0.0591 m. This indicates that immediate upward actuation is necessary. With the four tendons equally spaced from phase 0, channel 1 is the expected vertical-plane actuator. Its maximum 8 N force at the 0.023 m routing radius should provide substantial gravity cancellation and reveal the correct sign and useful holding level.

decision: Generate a substantially stiffer two-segment arm with the original 0.298 m straight-tip geometry, but change tendon topology to two root-only opposing tendons plus two full-length opposing tendons in the orthogonal plane. This preserves four independent channels while providing segment-selective shaping needed because M1_A requires large positive-z displacement with almost no x loss, unlike a single constant-curvature arc. Evaluate M1_A with a gradual full-span +z pull and low antagonistic bias to measure direction, attainable displacement, oscillation, and geometric-limit behavior.
evidence: Candidate c3 under channel-1 actuation confirmed that the +z-side tendon produces upward motion, but its compliant structure overshot to z=0.287 m at 0.30 s and ended with 0.986 m/s speed; tendon stroke reached [-0.0268,0.0252] m and tendon speed 0.1198 m/s. Thus stronger sections and slower loading are required. The targets also distinguish shape requirements: c3 starts at [0.298,0,0.150], while M1_A requests [0.295,0,0.215], a 65 mm transverse move with only 3 mm x reduction, motivating separate root and full-span authority rather than four identical full-span tendons. Expected outcome is much smaller oscillation and stroke, with channel 2 producing controlled positive-z bending; the run will establish whether stiffness is excessive or suitable before testing all conditions.

decision: Replace c4's segment-selective topology with four cardinal full-length tendons and reduce section stiffness to an intermediate level. c4 remained nearly straight and only moved about 20 mm downward under a 3.8 N differential, so it cannot cover M1_A's 65 mm upward displacement; c3 was reachable but excessively compliant. Four full-span cardinal tendons restore bidirectional y-z authority for all four required goals. Test M1_A using the tendon opposite c4's downward-producing +z route, with symmetric cocontraction and a gradual ramp intended to reduce the gravity transient and residual vibration.
evidence: c4 started at [0.298,0,0.150]. Its +z-side full-span channel produced negative-z motion and ended at z=0.12998 with only 4.35 mm maximum tendon stroke, showing ample stroke margin but excessive stiffness. Its 0.0734 m/s tendon speed and 0.4276 m/s hold-window tip speed show that a simple increasing ramp did not settle. Earlier c3 reached z=0.287 under upward actuation, proving reachability at lower stiffness but with excessive speed and stroke. Expected outcome for c5 is an upward response of intermediate magnitude, cardinal control authority in both transverse axes, and improved dynamic conditioning from intermediate stiffness, fewer cells, and symmetric tension.

decision: Probe the verified c5 structure with the opposite cardinal tendon before spending another candidate. The prior c5 test drove channel 3 above the common bias and produced strongly negative z; cardinal symmetry therefore predicts that driving channel 1 should produce positive z. Use lower common bias and a smaller differential, then hold from 0.30 s to expose the upward equilibrium and decay rate while reducing the prior stroke excursion.
evidence: The c5 M1_A run was valid and solver-stable. Channel-3 differential tension produced tip z values 0.0579 m at 0.14 s, 0.0354 m at 0.30 s, and 0.0124 m at 0.60 s, versus the 0.215 m target. Its terminal speed was only 0.0369 m/s despite a much larger 0.3017 m/s holding-window maximum, indicating oscillation rather than numerical failure. Reversing the cardinal differential should reverse the bending sign. Expected outcome is positive-z motion that identifies whether c5 can reach the target and supplies amplitude/phase evidence for a later input-shaped hold.

message.content: {"decision":"Create a substantially stiffer two-segment cardinal-routing design and immediately probe the physically correct +z tendon. The latest c5 test clarifies that channel 0 bends toward +y while gravity dominates z; with phase zero, channel 1 is therefore the +z actuator and channel 3 is the observed -z actuator. Maximum legal Young modulus should reduce the large oscillation and geometric tendon speed without changing the useful straight-pose reach.","evidence":"c5 starts at [0.298,0,0.15], nearly ideal in x for all goals. decision: Create a substantially stiffer two-segment cardinal-routing design and immediately probe the physically correct +z tendon. The latest c5 test clarifies that channel 0 bends toward +y while gravity dominates z; with phase zero, channel 1 is therefore the +z actuator and channel 3 is the observed -z actuator. Maximum legal Young modulus should reduce the large oscillation and geometric tendon speed without changing the useful straight-pose reach.
evidence: c5 starts at [0.298,0,0.15], nearly ideal in x for all goals. Its channel-0-biased run moved y positive to 0.0698 m at 0.30 s while z remained below the mount, confirming channel 0 is primarily +y rather than +z. Earlier c5 channel-3 excitation produced strongly negative z, consistent with cardinal phase ordering and identifying channel 1 as +z. c5 also showed 0.448 m/s holding speed and 0.0885 m/s tendon speed, so structural stiffness—not further large tension—is the immediate deficiency. Expected outcome is a smaller, cleaner upward response with legal stroke and materially lower speed, enabling condition-specific open-loop shaping.

decision: Create c7 with maximum legal square sections and maximum Young modulus, retaining the useful 0.298 m straight reach, then test M1_A using a smooth S-like rise of the confirmed +z channel. This isolates whether section stiffness plus gradual actuation can satisfy geometric speed and stroke limits while producing the required 65 mm lift.
evidence: c6 confirmed channel 1 raises z: at 0.30 s its tip reached z=0.2167 m, close to the M1_A target z=0.215 m. However, c6's prototype sections produced severe overshoot and violations: holding speed 0.247 m/s, tendon speed 0.165 m/s, and strokes about -25.7/+23.1 mm. Increasing only Young modulus was insufficient. The legal maximum 18 mm square sections should greatly increase bending stiffness relative to c6's smaller ellipse/tapered rectangle, reducing gravity sag, oscillation, and tendon excursion. A gradual, slope-shaped command reaching its plateau before the holding window should reduce excitation compared with c6's rapid piecewise ramp. Expected outcome is a slower monotonic lift with strokes below 15 mm and substantially lower terminal speed; the response amplitude will calibrate the final controls.

message.content: {"decision":"Retest c7 with an early gravity-compensation plateau followed by a delayed second tension increment. The objective is to prevent the large initial gravity sag that excited c7, while separating the final lift into two steps to reduce residual vibration during the holding window.","evidence":"In c7's first M1_A run, the robot fell from z=0.150 m to z=0.0946 m by 0.14 s because channel 1 had reached only 0.3875 N; this initial sag preceded the terminal oscillation and 0.230 m/s holding speed. At 0.30 s, with channel 1 at 2.7 N, the tip had recovered to z=0.1611 m with only 0.0166 m/s speed, showing that approximately 3 N can arrest and reverse gravity sag. Stroke remained safely within ±5.7 mm, leaving substantial geometric margin. Applying about 3 N almost immediately should keep the arm nearer its initial height, and a delayed increase to 4.6 N should produce the remaining upward bend without the continuously accelerating ramp that caused the prior overshoot. decision: Retest c7 with an early gravity-compensation plateau followed by a delayed second tension increment. The objective is to prevent the large initial gravity sag that excited c7, while separating the final lift into two steps to reduce residual vibration during the holding window.
evidence: In c7's first M1_A run, the robot fell from z=0.150 m to z=0.0946 m by 0.14 s because channel 1 had reached only 0.3875 N; this initial sag preceded the terminal oscillation and 0.230 m/s holding speed. At 0.30 s, with channel 1 at 2.7 N, the tip had recovered to z=0.1611 m with only 0.0166 m/s speed, showing that approximately 3 N can arrest and reverse gravity sag. Stroke remained safely within ±5.7 mm, leaving substantial geometric margin. Applying about 3 N almost immediately should keep the arm nearer its initial height, and a delayed increase to 4.6 N should produce the remaining upward bend without the continuously accelerating ramp that caused the prior overshoot. Expected outcome is reduced early excursion, lower tendon speed, and a terminal position closer to z=0.215 m; the trace will identify the usable plateau and timing for final condition-specific controls.

decision: Create c8 as a stiffer, shorter-neutral, isotropic two-segment arm and use the final exploratory physics run on M1_A before reserving four evaluations for all required conditions. The neutral tip is intended to lie near x=0.295 m, while reduced cell count and uniform square sections suppress flexible-mode excitation; a gradual single-channel ramp should avoid the abrupt transient seen on c7.
evidence: c7 began at x=0.298 m, so choosing segment lengths totaling 0.267 m instead of 0.270 m should place the straight tip near the M1_A target x=0.295 m. Its abrupt rise to 2.8 N by 0.02 s still produced 0.1115 m/s tip speed at 0.14 s, and the later stepped control ended with 0.1670 m/s tip speed and 0.0790 m/s tendon speed. Stroke was only about ±2.37 mm, showing ample force/stroke authority but inadequate transient control. c8 therefore uses maximum allowed material stiffness, uniform 14 mm square sections, six cells per segment, maximum routing radius, and a ramp spread over 0.40 s. Expected outcome is less gravity sag and substantially lower modal motion; the M1_A trace will determine whether this structure is suitable for the final four-condition evaluation.

decision: Use c7, the strongest observed candidate, for a complete authoritative evaluation on all four required conditions now, preserving one physics evaluation for a possible final targeted revision. Apply two-stage input-shaped tension profiles rather than the previously abrupt and later stepped M1_A command; use the polar tendon directions independently for each target.
evidence: Among valid own-run candidates, c7 has the lowest recorded maximum violation, 5.1956, versus c6 at 7.2307 and c8 at 16.8654. The prior c7 M1_A run used 2.8 N by 0.02 s and ended with 0.1670 m/s tip speed and 0.0790 m/s tendon speed, indicating useful authority but excessive residual vibration. c8 confirmed that a simple monotonic ramp can amplify oscillation, reaching 0.53596 m/s holding speed, so these controls instead introduce approximately half of the intended differential first and add the remainder later, while maintaining modest antagonist tension. Expected outcome is reduced residual vibration relative to the prior c7 control while producing upward bending for M1_A, negative-y/negative-z bending for M1_B and M5, and positive-y/positive-z bending for M1_C.
